The '''Clay Research Award''' is an annual award given by the Oxford-based [[Clay Mathematics Institute]] to [[mathematician]]s to recognize their achievements in mathematical research.  The following mathematicians have received the award:

{| class="wikitable sortable"
|-
! Year !! Winner !! Citation
|-
| 2026 || [[Robert Burklund]], [[Jeremy Hahn]],<br> [[Ishan Levy]] and [[Tomer Schlank]] <hr/>[[Yu Deng]] and [[Zaher Hani]] <hr/> [[Tuomas Orponen]], [[Pablo Shmerkin]], [[Hong Wang]] and [[Joshua Zahl]] || ”in recognition of their remarkable construction of counterexamples to Ravenel’s “Telescope Conjecture.” <hr/> "in recognition of their remarkable derivation of the Boltzmann equation for long times, starting from a system of hard spheres." <hr/> "in recognition of their remarkable work on geometric problems in harmonic analysis, leading to the proof of the Furstenberg set conjecture in the plane and the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions."
|-
| 2025 || not awarded
|-
| 2024 ||[[Paul Nelson (mathematician)|Paul Nelson]]<hr/>[[James Newton (mathematician)|James Newton]] and [[Jack Thorne (mathematician)|Jack Thorne]] || "in recognition of his groundbreaking contributions to the analytic theory of automorphic forms.  His work has resulted in the first convexity-breaking bounds for a large class of L-functions on the critical line (including all the standard ones of GL(n))." <hr/> "for their remarkable proof of the existence of the symmetric power functorial lift for Hilbert modular forms."
|-
| 2023 || [[Frank Merle (mathematician)|Frank Merle]],<br> [[Pierre Raphaël]],<br> [[Igor Rodnianski]] and <br> [[Jérémie Szeftel]] || "for their groundbreaking advances in the understanding of singular solutions to the fundamental equations of fluids dynamics, including their construction of smooth self-similar solutions for the compressible Euler equation, and families of finite-energy blow-up solutions for both the compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations."
|-
| 2022 ||[[Søren Galatius]] and [[Oscar Randal-Williams]] <hr/>[[John Pardon]]|| "for their profound contributions to the understanding of high dimensional manifolds and their diffeomorphism groups; they have transformed and reinvigorated the subject." <hr/> "in recognition of his wide-ranging and transformative work in geometry and topology, particularly his groundbreaking achievements in symplectic topology."
|-
| 2021 || [[Bhargav Bhatt (mathematician)|Bhargav Bhatt]] || "For his groundbreaking achievements in commutative algebra, arithmetic algebraic geometry, and topology in the p-adic setting."
|-
| 2020 || not awarded
|-
| 2019 ||  [[Wei Zhang (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]] <hr/>[[Tristan Buckmaster (mathematician)|Tristan Buckmaster]], [[Philip Isett]] and [[Vlad Vicol]] || "In recognition of his ground-breaking work in arithmetic geometry and arithmetic aspects of automorphic forms." <hr/> "In recognition of the profound contributions that each of them has made to the analysis of partial differential equations, particularly the Navier-Stokes and Euler equations."
|-
| 2018 || not awarded
|-
| 2017 || [[Aleksandr Logunov (mathematician)|Aleksandr Logunov]] and [[Eugenia Malinnikova]] <hr/> [[Jason Miller (mathematician)|Jason Miller]] and [[Scott Sheffield]] <hr/> [[Maryna Viazovska]] || "In recognition of their introduction of a novel geometric combinatorial method to study doubling properties of solutions to elliptic eigenvalue problems." <hr/> "In recognition of their groundbreaking and conceptually novel work on the geometry of the Gaussian free field and its application to the solution of open problems in the theory of two-dimensional random structures." <hr/> "In recognition of her groundbreaking work on sphere-packing problems in eight and twenty-four dimensions."
|-
| 2016 || [[Mark Gross (mathematician)|Mark Gross]] and [[Bernd Siebert]] <hr/>[[Geordie Williamson]] || "In recognition of their groundbreaking contributions to the understanding of [[Mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]], in joint work generally known as the ‘Gross-Siebert Program’" <hr/> "In recognition of his groundbreaking work in [[representation theory]] and related fields"
|-
| 2015 || [[Larry Guth]] and [[Nets Katz]] || "For their solution of the [[Erdős distinct distances problem|Erdős distance problem]] and for other joint and separate contributions to combinatorial [[incidence geometry]]"
|-
| 2014 || [[Maryam Mirzakhani]] <hr/> [[Peter Scholze]] || "For her many and significant contributions to geometry and [[ergodic theory]], in particular to the proof of an analogue of [[Ratner's theorems|Ratner's theorem]] on unipotent flows for moduli of flat surfaces." <hr/> "For his many and significant contributions to [[arithmetic algebraic geometry]], particularly in the development and applications of the theory of perfectoid spaces"
|-
| 2013 || [[Rahul Pandharipande]] || "For his recent outstanding work in [[enumerative geometry]], specifically for his proof in a large class of cases of the MNOP conjecture that he formulated with Maulik, [[Andrei Okounkov|Okounkov]] and Nekrasov"
|-
| 2012 || [[Jeremy Kahn]] and [[Vladimir Markovic]] || "For their work in [[hyperbolic geometry]]"
|-
| 2011 || [[Yves Benoist]] and [[Jean-François Quint]] <hr/> [[Jonathan Pila]] || "For their spectacular work on stationary measures and orbit closures for actions of [[Non-abelian group|non-abelian groups]] on [[Homogeneous space|homogeneous spaces]]" <hr/> "For his resolution of the [[André–Oort conjecture|André-Oort Conjecture]] in the case of products of [[Modular curve|modular curves]]"
|-
| 2010 || not awarded
|-
| 2009 || [[Jean-Loup Waldspurger]]  <hr/> [[Ian Agol]], [[Danny Calegari]] and [[David Gabai]] || "For his work in [[P-adic analysis|p-adic harmonic analysis]], particularly his contributions to the transfer conjecture and the [[Fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|fundamental lemma]]" <hr/> "For their solutions of the [[Marden tameness conjecture|Marden Tameness Conjecture]], and, by implication through the work of Thurston and Canary, of the [[Ahlfors measure conjecture|Ahlfors Measure Conjecture]]"
|-
| 2008 || [[Clifford Taubes]] <hr/> [[Claire Voisin]] || "For his proof of the [[Weinstein conjecture]] in dimension three" <hr/> "For her disproof of the Kodaira conjecture"
|-
| 2007 || [[Alex Eskin]] <hr/> [[Christopher Hacon]] and [[James McKernan]] <hr/> [[Michael Harris (mathematician)|Michael Harris]] and [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]] || "For his work on rational billiards and [[geometric group theory]], in particular, his crucial contribution to joint work with David Fisher and Kevin Whyte establishing the quasi-isometric rigidity of sol" <hr/> "For their work in advancing our understanding of the [[birational geometry]] of [[Algebraic variety|algebraic varieties]] in dimension greater than three, in particular, for their inductive proof of the existence of [[Flip (algebraic geometry)|flips]]" <hr/> "For their work on local and global [[Galois representations]], partly in collaboration with Clozel and Shepherd-Barron, culminating in the solution of the [[Sato–Tate conjecture|Sato-Tate conjecture]] for [[Elliptic curve|elliptic curves]] with non-integral [[J-invariant|j-invariants]]"
|-
| 2006 || not awarded
|-
| 2005 || [[Manjul Bhargava]] <hr/> [[Nils Dencker]] || "For his discovery of new composition laws for [[Quadratic form|quadratic forms]], and for his work on the average size of [[Ideal class group|ideal class groups]]" <hr/> "For his complete resolution of a conjecture made by [[François Trèves|F. Treves]] and [[Louis Nirenberg|L. Nirenberg]] in 1970"
|-
| 2004 || [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]] <hr/> [[Gérard Laumon]] and [[Ngô Bảo Châu]] || "For his joint work with [[Terence Tao|Terry Tao]] on [[Arithmetic progression|arithmetic progressions]] of [[Prime number|prime numbers]]" <hr/> "For their proof of the [[Fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|Fundamental Lemma]] for [[Unitary group|unitary groups]]"
|-
| 2003 || [[Richard S. Hamilton]] <hr/> [[Terence Tao]] || "For his discovery of the [[Ricci flow|Ricci Flow]] Equation and its development into one of the most powerful tools of [[geometric analysis]]" <hr/> "For his ground-breaking work in analysis, notably his optimal restriction theorems in [[Fourier analysis]], his work on the [[Wave maps equation|wave map equation]], his global existence theorems for [[Korteweg–de Vries equation|KdV type equations]], as well as significant work in quite distant areas of mathematics"
|-
| 2002 || [[Oded Schramm]] <hr/> [[Manindra Agrawal]] || "For his work in combining analytic power with geometric insight in the field of [[Random walk|random walks]], [[Percolation theory|percolation]], and [[probability theory]] in general, especially for formulating [[Schramm–Loewner evolution|stochastic Loewner evolution]]" <hr/> "For finding an algorithm that solves a modern version of a problem going back to the ancient Chinese and Greeks about how one can determine whether a number is prime in a [[Polynomial time|time that increases polynomially]] with the size of the number"
|-
| 2001 || [[Edward Witten]] <hr/> [[Stanislav Smirnov]] || "For a lifetime of achievement, especially for pointing the way to unify apparently disparate fields of mathematics and to discover their elegant simplicity through links with the physical world" <hr/> "For establishing the existence of the scaling limit of two-dimensional [[Percolation theory|percolation]], and for verifying [[John Cardy]]'s conjectured relation"
|-
| 2000 || [[Alain Connes]] <hr/> [[Laurent Lafforgue]] || "For revolutionizing the field of [[Operator algebra|operator algebras]], for inventing modern [[Noncommutative geometry|non-commutative geometry]], and for discovering that these ideas appear everywhere, including the foundations of theoretical physics" <hr/> "For his work on the [[Langlands program]]"
|-
| 1999 || [[Andrew Wiles]] || "For his role in the development of [[number theory]]"
|}
